findings.detail: The same actor has two names. The stem calls the code-writing actor "the agent" ("Your team uses the agent to write a converter"), but options A, B, C and D and their reasons call it "Claude". A reader may wonder whether these are two different actors. Use one name throughout.

blind_answer.reason: Test-driven iteration (3.5-K2/S2): writing a suite of expected behaviors, edge cases, and performance requirements before implementation and sharing failing test output catches regressions automatically, so each iteration builds on the last. A locks in current buggy behavior. B gives vague feedback. D discards progress and still relies on manual checks.
